question.text: A vertical assembly hangs together: a 2 kg block sits at the top and is pulled upward by a force F = 100 N. Below this block is a string of mass 2 kg, whose upper end is named A, whose lower end is named B, and whose exact midpoint is named C. A 4 kg block is tied to the string's lower end B. Work out the string tension at each of the points A, B and C.
conditions: string AB has its own mass, spread evenly along its length
an upward force F = 100 N acts on the 2 kg block at the top
a 4 kg block hangs from the string's lower end B
C is the exact midpoint of string AB

figure.description: A dashed outline encloses a vertical setup: at the top, a force of 100 N pulls upward, acting on a 2 kg block. Beneath that block hangs a string of mass 2 kg; its top end is A, its bottom end is B, and its midpoint is C. A 4 kg block hangs from end B. An upward arrow marks the acceleration a of the whole system.

solution.approach: Find the common upward acceleration of the whole system from the net force, then apply Newton's second law to whatever hangs below each labeled point.

steps.text: Find the acceleration of the whole system (top block, string, bottom block) from the net upward force.
The tension at A supports everything below A: the whole string and the bottom block.
The tension at C supports everything below C: half the string and the bottom block.
The tension at B supports only the bottom block below B, so T(A) = 75 N, T(C) = 62.5 N, T(B) = 50 N.

common_mistakes.text: Using the total system mass (8 kg) at every point instead of only the mass below each labeled point gives the same wrong tension, 100 N, everywhere.
Treating the string as massless drops its weight from the mass below A and C, giving T(A) = 50 N and T(C) = 50 N instead of 75 N and 62.5 N.
